claims.text: The Magere Brug, literally meaning Skinny Bridge, is a beautiful white-painted wooden bascule bridge stretching across the Amstel river.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The first bridge at this site was built in 1691 and had 13 arches, but it was so incredibly narrow that locals quickly nicknamed it the Skinny Bridge.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: However, recent research of city archives revealed that originally a broad and monumental stone bridge was planned during Amsterdam's prosperous Golden Age, but the 1672 economic setback forced the city council to drastically scale back the plans.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: A popular story told to tourists claims that the bridge was built by two sisters who lived on opposite sides of the Amstel river and wanted to be able to visit one another, every day.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The present bridge was built in 1934 and is decorated with 1,200 light bulbs which are turned on in the evening, creating a magical glow.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Locals regard the bridge as the most romantic of all in Amsterdam, making it a common site for proposals and lovers' strolls.
claims.subject: self
